subject: Communication
title: Framing: How the Same Story Changes Meaning
description: A fast breakdown of Framing: How the Same Story Changes Meaning for builders.

hook.text: 'Tax relief' vs. 'tax cuts for the wealthy.' Same policy. Different frame. Different public reaction. That's framing.

buildup.text: Framing is selecting certain aspects of reality and making them more prominent to promote a particular interpretation.

discovery.text: Kahneman and Tversky showed that framing a surgery as '90% survival' vs. '10% mortality' dramatically changed patient choices.

twist.text: All media is framed. There's no 'view from nowhere.' The question isn't whether framing exists, but whose frame you're seeing.

climax.text: Media-literate consumers don't just consume the frame. They identify it, consider alternatives, and ask who benefits.

punchline.text: Every story has a frame. See the frame, and you see the story differently.

quiz.question: What is media framing?
options: Selecting aspects of reality to promote a particular interpretation

details.summary: Framing theory shows that how information is presented fundamentally changes how people interpret it. Calling a policy a tax relief frames it as a burden being lifted. Calling it revenue reduction frames it as lost public resources. The facts are identical; the meaning changes entirely.
details.whyItMatters: Recognizing frames helps you see that seemingly objective reporting always contains interpretive choices that shape your understanding.
takeaways: Framing changes meaning without changing facts
Word choice, context, and emphasis all create frames
Every news story is framed whether or not creators intend it

faq.question: How can you detect framing in news coverage?
faq.answer: Read the same story from multiple outlets and notice different word choices, which experts are quoted, what context is included or omitted, and what metaphors are used. The differences reveal the frames. Also pay attention to headlines, which are the most concentrated framing devices.

faq.question: Is all framing manipulative?
faq.answer: No. Framing is inevitable in communication because every description requires choices about emphasis and context. The issue is not framing itself but unconscious or deliberately misleading framing. Good journalism makes its framing choices transparent and presents multiple frames.
